title: ConvSim Flyting Calibration Suite
description: Validates a flyting calibration file: reference volleys with the score band and gate outcome each one is expected to receive. Lives in a pack's calibration/ directory and is executed by scripts/flyting-calibration.py, which catches prompt and model drift before players do.

calibration_id.description: Unique identifier for this calibration suite within the pack.

scenario_id.description: The flyting scenario_id these volleys are scored against.

volleys.description: Reference volleys in ascending order of expected quality, by convention.

text.description: The volley exactly as a player would submit it.

note.description: Why this volley sits in its band — read by humans reviewing calibration failures.

expect.description: Assertions. Deterministic expectations (gate, flags, mechanics) are checked without a model; score bands and hooks additionally require a judge. At least one assertion is required, and every list-valued one must be non-empty: a block that asserts nothing would still cost a judge call, and the runner would report it as a pass.

gate.description: Stage 0 outcome. A dud scores 0 without a foul; a foul scores 0 and is recorded.

foul.description: The specific foul the volley must draw.

flags.description: Mechanical flags the volley must carry. 'judge_unavailable' is deliberately not offered: it is a property of the run rather than of the volley — present on every ungated volley of a judge-free run and on none of a judged one — so the runner skips it, and an entry whose only assertion was that flag would check nothing and report a pass.

band.description: Expected score band: dud = 0, weak = 1-59, solid = 60-119, strong = 120-179, highlight = 180+.

hooks.description: attack_surface trait ids the volley is expected to land, verified against the target NPC's declared surface.

judge_fouls.description: Register fouls the judge must raise. Unlike 'foul', which is a Stage 0 verdict and deterministic, these are read from the scene by the model, so they are only checked on a judged run. A raised foul zeroes the volley, so an entry using this usually pairs it with band: dud.
